meta.stem: You are the AED doctor. A 32-year-old woman, G2P1, 36+2 weeks, arrived by ambulance after a gush of fluid at home. The paramedic heard a slow fetal heart on their Doppler. She is on the trolley in Resus 2. Nurse is with her. Manage this patient.
meta.guidelineNotes:
Scoring truth is the OB-EM-01 exam script in this pack, not a rewritten guideline. Checked against RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 50 (2014; review extended December 2024) and the category-1 caesarean 30-minute decision-to-birth audit standard. Kept as written: do not replace the cord; minimal handling; loose warm saline gauze if the cord is outside; elevate the presenting part and keep the hand in; knee–chest in the bay; left lateral, head down, for transfer; bladder fill 500–750 mL only if birth will be delayed, then empty before caesarean; terbutaline 0.25 mg SC only if the fetal heart is still abnormal after elevation and birth will be delayed. RCOG also lists Trendelenburg beside knee–chest and left lateral. This mark scheme does not score Trendelenburg. RCOG does not recommend routine maternal oxygen. This script allows high-flow oxygen only if it does not delay, and it is not a scoring line. The source sheet is 100 marks, pass at least 70 with no critical hit. This gym ticks the observable lines from that sheet.

The bench randomises each run: the cord outside the introitus or only felt on examination, contractions or none, and in about one run in three the obstetric theatre is 20 minutes away. Then fill the bladder (Foley, 500–750 mL warm saline, clamp) and say it must be emptied before the caesarean; give terbutaline 0.25 mg SC only if contractions keep the heart abnormal and birth is delayed. The fetal heart on the strip drops while the cord is squeezed, recovers when you lift the head or fill the bladder, and dips for 15 seconds whenever the cord is handled. Your source notes suggest replacing the cord into the vagina and packing it; RCOG advises against handling or replacing it, so the bench scores that as a critical error.

marks.label: Introduce yourself, confirm name and HKID, and name the nurse
Privacy, chaperone, and ask the nurse to stay
Gloves and apron before you expose the perineum
Recognise overt cord prolapse aloud
Call for help immediately
Name the O&G on-call
Name labour ward and obstetric theatre
Name the anaesthetist
Name paediatrics and NICU
State category 1 caesarean and do not delay
Do not replace the cord
Minimal handling; loose warm saline gauze if the cord is outside
Manually elevate the presenting part
Keep that hand in until O&G takes over
Knee-chest position in the bay
Transfer left lateral, head down — not knee-chest on a trolley
Check the fetal heart and state the rate
Brief obstetric history that does not delay decompression
Maternal ABC without delaying decompression
Large-bore IV, group and save, and FBC without delaying decompression
Explain to the woman in plain language
Verbal consent for category 1 caesarean
Destination is labour-ward obstetric theatre
ISBAR handover including the times
Professional, concise, and speaking to the woman

actions.hint: Walk to the woman. Introduce yourself, confirm who she is, and get privacy.

options.label: I am Dr Chan, the emergency doctor. Name and HKID? This is Nurse Wong.
options.detail: You: Hello, my name is Dr Chan. I am the emergency doctor. Can I confirm your name and HKID? This is Nurse Wong. I need to look now — this can be an emergency for the baby.

options.label: Privacy screen, chaperone, nurse stays
options.detail: You pull the screen. Nurse Wong stays. You do not take a long history first.

options.label: Sit down for a full antenatal history before looking
options.detail: The cord is still compressed. A three-minute history is the common fail.

options.label: This is only a show — send her to the waiting hall
options.detail: Tissue at the introitus is cord until you look. The waiting hall is the wrong destination.

actions.hint: Tell Nurse Wong this is cord prolapse and to call for help now.

options.label: Obstetric emergency — call for help now
options.detail: Nurse Wong: Calling now. I will only call the teams you name.

options.label: Call psychiatry
options.detail: Psychiatry is not the team for cord prolapse.

options.label: Send her out for an ultrasound first
options.detail: Ultrasound in the waiting hall delays delivery. Look and decompress here.

actions.hint: Name O&G, labour-ward theatre, anaesthetics, and the baby doctor.

options.label: O&G on-call
options.detail: Nurse Wong: O&G on-call is being called.

options.label: Labour ward / obstetric OT
options.detail: Nurse Wong: Labour-ward theatre, not general ED theatre.

options.label: Anaesthetist
options.detail: Nurse Wong: Anaesthetist is being called.

options.label: Paediatrics / NICU
options.detail: Nurse Wong: The baby doctor is being called.

actions.hint: Say category 1 caesarean, 36 weeks, from AED. Do not delay.

options.label: Category 1 caesarean, 36 weeks, from AED — do not delay
options.detail: You: Tell them category 1 caesarean for cord prolapse, 36 weeks, coming from AED.

options.label: Category 3 — she can wait for a slot
options.detail: Cord prolapse with a live fetus is category 1. Waiting is a delay.

options.label: Book general ED theatre
options.detail: She needs labour-ward obstetric theatre, not general ED theatre.

actions.hint: Use the phone if you have not already named the teams.

options.label: O&G on-call
Labour ward / obstetric OT
Anaesthetist
Paediatrics / NICU
Category 1 caesarean, 36 weeks, from AED
Psychiatry
options.detail: Psychiatry is not the team for cord prolapse.

options.label: Send her to the waiting hall for an ultrasound
options.detail: That delay leaves the head on the cord.

options.label: General ED theatre
options.detail: Destination is labour-ward obstetric theatre.

actions.hint: Gloves and apron, expose, say it, lift the head off the cord and keep your hand in, loose warm gauze, knee–chest, Doppler, then left lateral head-down to move.

options.label: Hands on: relieve the cord now.
options.detail: The cord is decompressed.
options.performHint: Do it as you would on a real patient: look, lift, protect the cord, position, listen, plan for theatre, transfer. The fetal heart answers every move. Nothing stops a mistake; the debrief shows what to fix.

options.label: Push the cord back into the uterus
options.detail: The cord looks paler. The fetal heart falls further. Do not replace it.

options.label: Instrumental birth here — cervix is only 4 cm
options.detail: Cervix is about 4 cm. Vaginal birth in ED is for full dilatation with someone who can deliver now, not this case.

options.label: Ask her to walk to theatre
options.detail: Walking drops the head back onto the cord.

actions.hint: One minute of facts while the hand stays in. Do not start with a long history.

options.label: Contractions, bleeding, singleton, praevia, meal, allergies, previous CS
options.detail: Contracting 1 in 3. No heavy bleeding. Singleton, cephalic. No praevia, no previous caesarean. Last meal two hours ago. No allergies. Cervix about 4 cm — you do not stop elevation to re-examine.

options.label: Full booking history before you touch her
options.detail: Three minutes of history with the head still on the cord.

options.label: Ask the nurse, not the woman
options.detail: She is distressed and she can talk. Speak to her.

actions.hint: Quick maternal ABC. Do not lie her flat and do not drop the presenting part.

options.label: Talking, RR, SpO2, pulse, BP. Left tilt if she is not knee-chest.
options.detail: She talks in sentences. RR, SpO2, pulse and BP are stable. You do not move the elevating hand to do it. High-flow oxygen only if it does not delay — weak evidence, not a scoring line.

options.label: Lie her flat on her back for a full set of obs
options.detail: Flat on her back puts the head back on the cord.

options.label: Full maternal workup before calling anyone
options.detail: ABC is a glance. It does not come before help or elevation.

actions.hint: A second pair of hands can site a large-bore IV and send G&S and FBC. Do not drop the head to do it yourself.
actions.prompt: IV trolley — only if it does not delay
actions.confirmLabel: Ask the second pair to do this

options.label: Large-bore cannula, second pair of hands
options.performHint: Drag the cannula to her arm. Do not take the elevating hand away.

options.label: Group and save, and FBC
Wait for the blood results before leaving
options.detail: Do not delay transfer for bloods.

options.label: Take my hand out and site the cannula myself
options.detail: The head drops back onto the cord. Someone else sites the drip.

actions.hint: Explain in plain language and take verbal consent for the category 1 caesarean.

options.label: The cord is in front of the head. Emergency caesarean now. I come with my hand in.
options.detail: You: The baby's cord has come down in front of the head after your waters broke. The head can squeeze the cord and the baby can lose oxygen. I am holding the head off the cord. You need an emergency caesarean in obstetric theatre now. I will come with my hand in place. The obstetric, anaesthetic and baby doctors are on the way. This is category 1 — we aim to deliver within 30 minutes.

options.label: BB嘅臍帶跌咗出嚟，要即刻剖腹
options.detail: You: BB嘅臍帶跌咗出嚟，頭會压住條帶，BB會缺氧。我而家用手托住個頭。要即刻去手術室剖腹，目標三十分鐘內出世。

options.label: Verbal consent is enough. Any questions? Who should we call?
options.detail: You: For a category 1 caesarean, verbal consent is enough. Do you understand? Any questions? Who should we call for you?

options.label: Full written consent booklet before we move
options.detail: Written consent delays a category 1 caesarean. Verbal consent is enough.

actions.hint: The partner can come if she wants.

options.label: You can come to obstetric theatre if she wants
options.detail: Partner: I'll come. You keep your hand in.

options.label: Wait downstairs, we will phone
options.detail: She asked who to call. Sending the partner away without asking her is the colder version.

actions.hint: Move as one unit to labour-ward theatre. Left lateral, head down, hand stays in.

options.label: Labour-ward OT as one unit. Left lateral, head down, hand stays in.
options.detail: You: Nurse, we move as one unit to labour-ward OT, not general ED OT. Left lateral, head down, my hand stays in. Bring notes, Doppler, oxygen, and the partner if she wants.

options.label: General ED theatre
options.detail: ED theatre is the wrong destination.

options.label: Roll her all-fours down the corridor
options.detail: Knee-chest is for the bay. The corridor and the lift are left lateral, head down.

options.label: Take my hand out for the lift
options.detail: If the hand comes out, the head drops back onto the cord.

actions.hint: ISBAR, state the times, and do not take the hand out until O&G takes over.

options.label: ISBAR and the four times. Hand stays until O&G takes over.
options.detail: You: I am Dr Chan from AED. Situation: overt cord prolapse. Background: 32-year-old, G2P1, 36+2, SROM at home, singleton, no previous CS, last meal two hours ago, no allergies. Assessment: cord visible, I have elevated the presenting part continuously, mother stable, fetal heart 80 and ongoing. Recommendation: category 1 caesarean under O&G now; paediatric team for neonatal resuscitation; paired cord gases after birth. Times: diagnosis, help called, elevation started, left AED. I will write the notes and an incident form. We debrief her after delivery, when she is ready. I do not remove my hand until O&G takes over.

options.label: Take my hand out now that we have arrived
options.detail: The head drops onto the cord. The hand stays until O&G takes over or the baby is out.

options.label: Write a long note before anyone else touches her
options.detail: Document the times, but do not delay the handover to write an essay.

actions.hint: If the examiner asks, answer from the script.

options.label: Why not replace the cord?
options.detail: Vasospasm, and no good evidence. RCOG does not recommend replacing it.

options.label: Why knee-chest, then Sims?
options.detail: Knee-chest lifts the presenting part most while you are still in the bay. Sims, left lateral and head down, is the safe position on a moving trolley.

options.label: When would birth be vaginal?
options.detail: Full dilatation and birth immediately and safely, by someone who can do an instrumental delivery. Not by the ED at 4 cm.

options.label: Bladder fill — how much, and when?
options.detail: 500–750 mL warm saline through a Foley, only if theatre is delayed. Empty the bladder immediately before caesarean.

actions.hint: Tocolysis and the preterm branch, if asked.

options.label: Terbutaline — dose and rule?
options.detail: Terbutaline 0.25 mg subcutaneous if the fetal heart is still abnormal after elevation and there is a delay. Do not leave the patient to find it.

options.label: What about 24–26 weeks?
options.detail: Consultant O&G and neonatology counsel on survival versus expectant care. You still decompress while they decide.

options.label: Replacing the cord is safer
options.detail: That is the opposite of the script. The cord looks paler when you push it back.

options.label: Fill the bladder with 200 mL now, every time
options.detail: 500–750 mL, and only if there is a delay. Not 200 mL, and not before a ready theatre.

sequenceRules.okNote: Help called before the history and the drip — acceptable.
sequenceRules.failNote: History or IV before calling for help. The examiner expects the emergency call first.

sequenceRules.okNote: Decompression before history and lines — acceptable.
sequenceRules.failNote: History, ABC, or a cannula before the presenting part was elevated.

sequenceRules.okNote: The hand was in before handover.
Knee-chest in the bay before the transfer plan.
sequenceRules.failNote: Transfer plan before positioning in the bay.
